title: Dian Fossey's birth chart
metaDescription: Dian Fossey's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 25.5° Capricorn. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Four of the nine placements whose signs are settled stand in Capricorn — the Sun, Mercury, Mars and Saturn. The placements whose signs could change with an unknown hour are not counted. A cluster that size becomes the section the rest of the chart plays around.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: At the noon reference the Sun sits 25.5° into Capricorn — the third decan, which the old scheme hands to Mercury. Same sign, different decan, different chart.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: Day to day the chart speaks through Mercury in Capricorn (2.8°), Venus in Aquarius (27.2°), Mars in Capricorn (29.1°): thought with its feet on the ground, attraction that begins as conversation, effort banked steadily until it tells.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The day's firmest angle joins the Sun and Saturn — a conjunction holding at 0.1°. The tradition stops reading a conjunction as two things. It is one appetite with two names, and it moves together or not at all. Behind it, Mars conjunction Saturn at 3.4°, and the Sun conjunction Mars at 3.6° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. The unknown hour cannot unmake any of this: every aspect named survived all twenty-five samples of the day.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: No closed figure — no grand trine, t-square, or grand cross — holds among the day-stable angles. The chart distributes its tension pair by pair rather than through one standing structure.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The dignity table, which predates the outer planets and only ever spoke for seven, marks two placements here. Mars in Capricorn at 29.1° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Saturn in Capricorn at 25.6° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules. The table describes circumstance rather than quality — a planet in detriment is inconvenienced, not diminished.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Among the 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the elements divide 5 earth, 2 fire, 1 air, 1 water; by modality, 6 cardinal, 2 fixed, 1 mutable. Earth weights a chart toward the material and the durable — what can be built, kept, and relied on. Jupiter, Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — apparent backward motion from where the Earth sits, which the tradition reads as a function turned inward before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Aries into Taurus during that day at the birthplace, travelling 11.9° between one midnight and the next. Half the day belongs to each sign, and the split falls at an unrecorded hour — so this page holds the Moon as a genuine unknown.
